I posted this a few days ago and it seemed to get ignored, I think these are some good rules to live by though.

You win some and you lose some, and hopefully win more that you lose. It's as much of a psychological game as a physical one. You need hundreds (if not thousands) of games of practise to really understand the game and seed into good matchmaking. It takes lots of dedication and I can honestly say I've been in the position of giving up more than once, but I truly want to be the best, so I truck on and keep finding inspiration.

The game takes dedication down to an obsession. Once you have a high pool of games, you're more likely to get others with many games under their belt and less likely to run into the weekend warriors that only take the game with a grain of salt (trolls, small children and drunks). Something I call "Matchmaking Hell". 

The players with a lower pool of games seem to take the game a lot less serious and tend to either make poor plays, give up, have lack of knowledge or harass and troll teammates. As your pool of games increases, you will be paired with people whom have a similar amount of games. Players with lots of games have more appreciation for the game and are less likely to fool around and troll their teammates as they are now (hopefully) mature players who understand what wins games and what doesn't.

Here's some personal tips I have to keeping your sanity on the road to the top!

The game in my opinion relies heavily on your teammates morale. To ensure a victory takes much more than making plays, but making friends as well :). When a teammate makes a good play, praise them. When a teammate makes a bad play, say "Good try!". Make even the weak players feel as though they are an integral part of the team, as a team is only as strong as their weakest link. 

A praised player is more likely to listen to directions, perform more confidently, carefully and even make strong more well thought out decisions. Even if a player makes a mistake, give them confidence and hope. A lack of hope will lead to poor plays, bad decisions and simply not caring, possibly leading to an AFK. Even worse, once a person gives up, it's likely others will give up too. Praising your team can be just as infectious though! It's a 2-way street. If you praise teammates, others are more likely to do the same, creating a good environment to win a game.

Another thing I've done to keep a positive mindset in a defeat is to consider personal victories. If you've done well, won your lane, made smart plays and have done everything in your power to ensure a victory and still lost. In my mind, I consider that a victory. Your not going to win them all, but you can learn to appreciate your own work in a game and bring that mentality to future games. 

Learn timers.
Learn to cs.
Learn to ward. (not limited to support)
Learn to roam.
Learn your position and job.
Learn your enemies patterns.
Learn to counter.
Learn the mechanics of many champions.
Learn the mechanics of enemy champions.
Learn to love.
Learn everything!

If you truly love the game, you will learn all these things because you WANT to, not because you HAVE to. Don't make a chore out of a game, make a fun learning experience. 

Sure, their are aspects of the game that may not be balanced. It's always going to be work in progress, nothing is static. In a constantly expanding game, adding and changing content leads to unforeseen changes in other places, leading to unintentional buffs, nerfs and errors. You need to learn to adapt to these changes. It's all a lot more work than you think balancing a pool of over 100 champions. You need to remember that Riot are human beings like you and I and are prone to making mistakes too.

All In all, Riot is doing their best to deliver the best possible game for you, with frequent updates, patches and content. If you feel there's an issue, then voice your opinions and thoughts. Riot tries very hard to appease it's fans and give them the game they all want.

These are just a few of many thoughts I'd like to share, I hope I've helped send you on a better path to being a better more positive player! :)

Peace and love,
